source.section: PDF p10-11 Line 4 'What pensions are exempt?' third bullet (noncontributory U.S. uniformed services pension); Form 1 lines 2a, 4, 10-22

worked: Federal AGI = U.S. Army retired pay (noncontributory military pension) 30,000.00 (person 0) + private pension 45,000.00 (person 1) = 75,000.00 (given). Federal taxable income = 75,000.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction (31,500.00) = 43,500.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Massachusetts Form 1 (the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt items): Line 4 taxable pensions = 0.00 for the 30,000.00 U.S. Army retired pay (noncontributory military pension) (exempt: noncontributory U.S. uniformed services pension, PDF p10-11 third bullet) + 45,000.00 private pension (taxed: most private pensions are taxable, PDF p10) = 45,000.00. Line 10 total 5.0% income = 45,000.00. Line 16 total deductions = 0.00. Line 17 = 45,000.00 - 0.00 = 45,000.00. Line 2a personal exemption (married_joint) = 8,800.00; line 2c age 65 or over before 2026: 0 x 700.00 = 0.00; line 2g = line 18 = 8,800.00. Line 19 = 45,000.00 - 8,800.00 = 36,200.00. Line 20 interest and dividends = 0.00. Line 21 = 36,200.00. Line 22 = 36,200.00 x 0.05 = 1,810.00. No 8.5%/12% income or long-term gains (lines 23-24 = 0.00); 4% surtax 0.00 (line 21 is under 1,083,150). Line 28 total tax = 1,810.00; no credits (No Tax Status and the Limited Income Credit do not apply: Massachusetts AGI 45,000.00 is over their limits). State income tax = 1,810.00.
